errorCodes.meaning: The document exceeds the maintainer's stated per-record cap. The cap and the actual size are both returned, so a producer can tell how far over it is rather than guessing.
Annotating form only — no contact exists at `contactId` in this context. Answered the same whether the identifier was never assigned or belongs to another context.
An identifier in `lists` names no list in this context. Nothing is changed. A producer creates the list with persona/contact/lists/put first.

ClaimType.description:
The vocabulary token naming what a value IS — `name.legal`, `phone.mobile`, `address.postal`, `person.birthDate`. Dotted, most-general segment first, so that a consumer with no knowledge of the specific token can still group by its prefix.

The token is the maintainer's own; no external vocabulary is primary. External vocabularies (vCard/jCard, OIDC standard claims, schema.org) are mappings applied at PRESENTATION by a renderer, not at rest, so that a query written in any of them can be matched without the store having to live inside any one of them.

The `x:` prefix is an open extension namespace and is not decoration. The closest prior art — Windows CardSpace's self-issued card — supported exactly fifteen predefined claim types with no extensibility, and that is the specific way it failed the requirement a holder actually has. An `x:` attribute stores, composes, binds and discloses exactly like a known one; it renders generically and matches only an explicit query.
ClaimType.title: ClaimType

ContactDocument.description: What a peer disclosed, as received. Structurally the same claim set a holder composes and presents — a profile and a contact card are one schema seen from two sides — which is why a maintainer validates both with the same code and a consumer renders both with the same view.

cardVersion.description: The publisher's own monotonic counter, if they supplied one. Advisory: it orders the publisher's revisions relative to each other and MUST NOT be trusted to order them against anything else.

provenance.description: As asserted by the publisher. A recipient MUST NOT treat a claimed credentialBacked provenance as verified — it is a statement about what the publisher says backs the claim, and verification is a separate act against the credential itself.

publisher.description: The DID that published the document, as it appeared. Normally a pairwise identifier, so it names the relationship rather than the person.

ContactDocument.title: ContactDocument

DirectoryEntryId.description: A community directory entry's identifier, exactly as that community's directory returned it. Opaque and community-scoped: the agent stores and compares it as a string, never parses it, and never treats the same value under two communities as the same entry.
DirectoryEntryId.title: DirectoryEntryId

DirectoryRef.description: Links a contact to the entry in a community's member directory it corresponds to, so the holder's own client can join that community's directory with the holder's address book — showing a star or a petname beside an entry — without either side telling the other. The community never learns the link exists; the contact never learns it either. A contact has at most one.

entryId.description: The entry, as that community's directory identifies it.

vtcDid.description: The DID of the community whose directory holds the entry.

DirectoryRef.title: DirectoryRef

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

ListId.description: Identifier of one of the holder's contact lists: a ULID in Crockford base32, uppercase, assigned by the agent when the list is created. Meaningful only inside the context that holds the list; it is never sent to anyone but the holder's own clients.
ListId.title: ListId

ListIds.description: The lists a contact is on, as a set: order carries no meaning. A contact on no list has no `lists` member, never an empty array, so there is one way to say "none".
ListIds.title: ListIds

Petname.description: The holder's private name for a contact, on one line: no control characters, line breaks included. A petname in Zooko's sense — chosen by the holder, meaningful to the holder, and unforgeable by anyone else, because nobody else can write it. Distinct from the contact's own disclosed `nickname` or display name, which the contact chose and may change. Compared exactly, as a string: an agent does not case-fold or normalise it.
Petname.title: Petname

ProofRung.description:
How strongly a credential-backed claim is hidden when presented, ordered most private first. `predicate` proves a statement over a claim without disclosing the claim. `derived` discloses exactly the claims needed via an unlinkable derived proof, so two presentations cannot be joined. `selectiveDisclosure` discloses exactly the claims needed but carries the issuer's signature unchanged, so two presentations ARE linkable. `whole` discloses the entire credential.

The distinction between the first two and the last two is of kind, not degree: only `predicate` and `derived` avoid handing two verifiers a join key. A maintainer MUST default to the highest rung the credential's format supports, and MUST NOT silently fall to a lower one — a request that cannot be satisfied at the rung a producer asked for is refused, because a silent privacy downgrade discloses material the holder believed was hidden.
ProofRung.title: ProofRung

Provenance.description:
Where a value comes from, and the member that makes this family worth building on a trust stack rather than in an address book. It survives to the verifier, so a recipient can tell — per field — what the holder typed from what an issuer attested.

`selfAsserted` — the holder supplied it.

`credentialBacked` — the value is derived from a credential in the vault at `claimPath`. The stored value is a CACHE FOR DISPLAY; the credential is the truth. A maintainer MUST re-derive it on read and MUST fail closed (never presenting a stale value) when the credential has been revoked, has expired, or has been archived or deleted.

`generated` — the value is minted per verifier at disclosure time and recorded against that verifier, so every relying party receives a different one that routes back to the holder. This is the shape of the most widely adopted consumer privacy feature in this space; a maintainer need not operate a relay to conform, but the shape must exist, because retrofitting per-verifier values into a pool-of-values model is a migration rather than an addition.

`derived` — the value was taken from a source the holder connected or supplied — a code-hosting profile, an uploaded CV — rather than typed by them or attested by an issuer. Nobody signed it: it is the holder's claim that the source said so, and a consumer MUST NOT present it as attested. It exists as its own kind because a derived value is neither of the others — the holder did not author it, and no one vouches for it — and a holder deciding whether to disclose deserves to know which of their values they typed.

For how strongly a disclosed value identifies the holder, the kinds rank `credentialBacked` above `derived` above `selfAsserted`; `generated` values are per-verifier and do not correlate.

claimPath.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the claim within the credential, e.g. `/credentialSubject/familyName`.

credentialId.description: Vault identifier of the backing credential.

issuerDid.description: Issuer of the backing credential. Advisory: a consumer MUST verify the credential rather than trusting this member.

proof.description: The disclosure rung this claim was, or will be, presented at.

generator.description: Names the minting scheme, e.g. `relayEmail`. Maintainer-defined.

perVerifier.description: When true (the default and the only useful setting), a distinct value is minted for each verifier.

derivedAt.description: When the value was taken from the source. A derived value is a snapshot: the source may have changed since, and nothing re-derives it.

source.description: The KIND of source the value was taken from — `github`, `cvUpload`, `linkedIn` — never an account, handle or URL. Provenance survives to the verifier, so this member is disclosed with the claim; a handle here would disclose an identifier the holder never chose to share.

Provenance.title: Provenance

Response.description: Success response to persona/contact/put. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/persona/contact/put/1.2#response. Identifiers, the current revision and what changed; no claim value and no annotation text is echoed.

annotationsChanged.description: True when any annotation now differs from what was stored. False when every annotation given already matched and every one named for removal was already absent — including a filing that named none.

changedClaims.description: Claim types whose value differs from the previous revision. Present only on a filing that updated an existing contact.

rev.description: The contact's current revision: the one a filing just appended, or, for an annotating request, the revision that was already current. Annotations never move it.

wasCreated.description: True when this is the first revision for the subject. Always false for an annotating request.

Ulid.description: A ULID in Crockford base32, uppercase. Used for `attributeId` and `profileId`. Server-assigned on create; a producer MAY supply one to make a create idempotent, and a maintainer MUST reject a supplied value that already exists rather than silently overwriting.

schema.description: File what a peer disclosed, or change the holder's own annotations on a contact, or both. Three forms. FILING (`subjectDid`, `knownByPersona`, `document`; no `contactId`) appends a revision, never overwrites, so a changed value is visible as a change rather than arriving silently — exactly as 1.0. ANNOTATING (`contactId`; no `subjectDid`, `knownByPersona`, `document` or `credentialRefs`) changes the holder's star, petname, lists, directory link or notes on an existing contact and appends no revision. LINKING (`directoryRef`, `knownByPersona`; no `contactId`, `subjectDid`, `document` or `credentialRefs`) keeps annotations on a member of a community's directory whose DID the holder has not been shown: it finds, or makes, the contact for that entry and persona, and appends no revision. In every form each annotation given replaces the stored one, each `removeX` removes one, and each annotation absent is unchanged. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

contactId.description: Annotating form only: the existing contact whose annotations change. A filing never names one — the agent keys a filing on (contextId, subjectDid, knownByPersona) as in 1.0.

credentialRefs.description: Filing form only. Vault identifiers of credentials the peer presented alongside the document. The credentials themselves belong in the credential vault and the contact holds references.

directoryRef.description: Link the contact to a community directory entry, replacing any link it had. Absent: unchanged.

knownByPersona.description: Filing and linking forms. Which of the holder's personas knows this contact. A contact belongs to the relationship, not to the holder at large — the same peer met through two personas is two contacts, and collapsing them would correlate the holder's own personas in their own address book.

lists.description: The lists the contact is on, replacing the whole set. Every identifier MUST name a list in this context. Absent: unchanged. Take the contact off every list with `removeLists`.

notes.description: The holder's private note about this contact, replacing any they had. Absent: unchanged. Never disclosed to anyone, including the contact.

petname.description: The holder's private name for the contact, replacing any they had. Absent: unchanged.

removeDirectoryRef.description: Remove the contact's directory link. Only `true` is accepted.

removeLists.description: Take the contact off every list. Only `true` is accepted.

removeNotes.description: Remove the note. Only `true` is accepted.

removePetname.description: Remove the petname. Only `true` is meaningful, so only `true` is accepted. A separate member rather than `petname: null`, because a nullable optional member makes "unchanged" and "remove" the same value in libraries that map both to one absent option.

starred.description: Star or unstar the contact. Absent: unchanged. A boolean rather than a remove member because `false` is a value the holder chose, not an absence.

subjectDid.description: Filing form only. The DID the document is about, as disclosed. Normally pairwise, so it names this relationship and not the person across all of theirs.

schema.title: Persona Contact Put — payload
